design_references.idea: Offline weight/scale layout, maximum-width loads, activation reuse, double buffering, tile scheduling. Investigate IQ codebook formats feeding Intel XMX without full FP16 expert expansion.
Separate memory layout from external format; tile for cache and ISA, reuse quantized weights across routed tokens. Ryzen lacks AMX; adapt the layout principle to AVX2/XMX.
Choose CPU computation versus transferring expert weights according to measured cost; relevant to current heterogeneous executor.
Shape-specific fused MoE kernels, routing/grouping and quantization fusion. Inspect implementations, benchmark each transferred idea.
CPU matrix layouts and multirow quantized products; evaluate AVX2-specific implementation rather than infer benefit from AVX512 results.

xmx_prompt_experiment.linear_persistent_conclusion: Prefill and decode cancellation/recovery passed, but repeat-writing generated IDs diverged at index 11. This is not an equivalent-output throughput comparison; XMX remains opt-in.

exact_large_state_screen.conclusion: All compared output bits matched; MMQ slower than the preceding kernel. Rejected as a performance candidate.

exact_one_vector_microbenchmark.conclusion: All compared outputs were bit-identical. Per-component timings are screening evidence only.

rejected_link_split_screen.conclusion: First off run contains large first-use compilation costs and is not a steady-state paired baseline. Reverted the global linker change before further end-to-end comparisons.

xmx_prompt_experiment.exact_persistent_conclusion: All completed request IDs matched the Zen 3 baseline, including repeat writing; prefill/decode cancellation and eight-token recovery passed. Repeated decode rates 15.98/20.25 tok/s are one screen, not an established gain. First writing prompt 7511.1 ms versus prior baseline 3571.4 ms needs separate first-use evaluation; no serving configuration changed.
